description: New Star Tech is an independent student-led technology initiative focused on AI, software engineering, and practical innovation. For NASA Space Apps 2026, its proposed HarborShield AI project explores NASA Earth-observation data, coastal environmental trends, maritime disaster risks, pollution prevention, and port recovery intelligence. The goal is to develop an explainable, human-supervised prototype that supports safer operations, environmental protection, and informed decisions.
summary:
HarborShield AI is a coastal environmental intelligence platform designed to make NASA Earth science data more accessible, interpretable, and actionable for scientific investigation and maritime resilience.

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, the prototype addresses “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” by providing a unified workspace for investigating long-term environmental changes across coastal regions.

The system integrates NASA POWER meteorological datasets, including temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. It supports historical time-series analysis, annual aggregation, statistical trend estimation, confidence intervals, significance testing, and comparisons between coastal locations.

Initially focused on India's Bay of Bengal coastline, HarborShield AI aims to reduce the manual effort involved in retrieving, processing, comparing, and interpreting fragmented environmental information.

Its broader vision is to support researchers, coastal planners, port authorities, and maritime professionals through transparent, evidence-based environmental intelligence.

Rather than replacing professional judgment, HarborShield AI is designed to improve analytical efficiency, preserve scientific traceability, and support more informed environmental and operational decisions.
details:
HarborShield AI is a coastal environmental intelligence platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”

The project investigates long-term environmental changes in coastal regions using NASA Earth science data. Its initial prototype focuses on three locations along India's Bay of Bengal coastline: Haldia, Paradip, and Visakhapatnam.

How It Works

HarborShield AI retrieves real historical environmental observations through the NASA POWER Monthly Point API.

The prototype currently supports three environmental variables:

- Near-surface air temperature (T2M)

- Corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR)

- Wind speed at 10 metres (WS10M)

Users select a coastal location, environmental variable, and historical period between 2001 and 2024.

The application retrieves NASA observations, filters missing values, aggregates monthly observations into annual averages, and calculates environmental trends using ordinary least squares (OLS) regression.

Statistical outputs include trend slopes, two-sided Student-t p-values, 95% confidence intervals, and the number of complete annual observations.

An interactive dashboard displays historical changes and estimated trend lines. Users can compare trends between coastal locations and export observations and analytical evidence.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Coastal environmental investigations often require retrieving, processing, and interpreting datasets across multiple locations and time periods.

HarborShield AI simplifies this process through a unified analytical interface.

The intended benefits include improved accessibility to NASA Earth science information, reproducible environmental investigations, easier regional comparisons, and more transparent interpretation of historical environmental patterns.

Its longer-term vision is to support coastal researchers, maritime professionals, port authorities, and environmental planners with evidence-based intelligence for understanding environmental exposure and supporting resilience planning.

Technologies Used

The prototype uses:

- NASA POWER Monthly Point API for Earth science observations.

- JavaScript for application logic and statistical analysis.

- Cloudflare Workers for the server-side application architecture and local development.

- HTML, CSS, and SVG for the user interface and trend visualizations.

- Node.js and automated tests for development and verification.

AI-assisted development tools, including OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex, were used for technical planning, code generation, debugging, and review. The current verified environmental analysis is deterministic rather than dependent on an operational generative AI service.

Creativity and Innovation

HarborShield AI combines NASA environmental data retrieval, statistical analysis, regional comparison, visualization, and evidence export within a single coastal-focused workflow.

Rather than presenting isolated weather observations, the prototype helps users investigate historical patterns and evaluate whether apparent changes are statistically distinguishable from ordinary variation under conventional regression assumptions.

Its design emphasizes scientific traceability, transparent calculations, and understandable results.

Design Considerations and Limitations

The prototype prioritizes reliable NASA data integration, missing-data handling, complete-year validation, reproducible calculations, and explicit uncertainty reporting.

NASA POWER observations are gridded or model-derived estimates rather than direct measurements at port facilities.

The regression methodology assumes independent residuals; temporal autocorrelation, outliers, and other statistical limitations may affect significance estimates.

The current prototype does not predict cyclone occurrence, port downtime, oil spills, or economic losses. These represent possible future research directions rather than implemented capabilities.

HarborShield AI is intended to support environmental investigation and informed human judgment, not replace scientific expertise or operational decision-making.
